objective: Extraction core: provider contract, wire schema and strict local validator, prompt with random delimiters, deterministic bilingual fake, budget/rate/concurrency gate in integer micro-dollars, opt-in rephrase guard.
context: Built against spec.md (AI / LLM Design, Internal module contracts), decision OQ-D7 (customer share default 0.2, the NFR6 test pins 1) and the brief's RS-01, RS-02, RS-03, RS-05 and NFR6. No real model call is made; every result below comes from the deterministic fake provider and is evidence of the harness and the pipeline, NOT of model quality (the live-model suite is LIVE-M1, not part of this task). src/ai imports only src/domain (AppError, localDay, buildQuestions) and node built-ins; the DB and the clock are injected into the gate. The provenance enum on the wire is the spec's user_text|image|none (manual is assigned by the confirm step, SEC-8).

Contract notes for d3 (src/services/extraction.js and src/main.js): (1) gate = createGate({db, clock, limits: gateLimitsFromConfig(config)}); the gate reads config fields modelDailyBudgetMicroUsd, modelCallCapMicroUsd, fakeModelCostMicroUsd (integers, preferred) and falls back to the existing modelDailyBudgetUsd, modelCallCapUsd, fakeModelCostUsd; modelCustomerDailyShare is already parsed (default 0.2). d3 may add the three micro fields to config.js with toMicroUsd(raw env string), or leave config.js unchanged; both work. (2) Call order: gate.takeRate(customerId) on every image upload; extraction = gate.run({customerId, requestId, call: () => provider.extract({text, image, signal})}) which takes the rate, reserves the cap, calls outside any transaction, settles with usage.costMicroUsd (or costUsd) and refunds on a thrown error. A refusal throws a domain AppError (429 RATE_LIMITED details.limit extract_upload|model_concurrency with headers['Retry-After'], or 503 MODEL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED details.scope global|customer) that the HTTP layer adopts via adoptAppError; d3 stores the degraded row in a separate transaction. (3) The fake takes faults: () => null|'timeout'|'invalid_json'|'schema_invalid'|'error' (a 'fake_model:' prefix is accepted); d3 must read and decrement the fake_model:* row of fault_flags and return the fault name, because adapters never touch service tables. (4) createFakeProvider({costMicroUsd}) takes integer micro-dollars: pass toMicroUsd(config.fakeModelCostUsd). (5) On ProviderError use toDegraded(err) for {schemaOk:false, degraded:true, errorCode, output: all unknown}. (6) validateExtraction(output, {text, imageNumbers}) rejects ungrounded output (provider adapters should call parseAndValidate with the request text); the spec's post-validation normalisation (downgrade to unknown, ranges, image wording stripping, non-USD budget) stays in services/extraction.js and is not implemented here. (7) renderQuestions(output.questions) gives the server-templated Question[].

Contract notes for d2: the fake image map is keyed by sha256 hex of the image bytes (not by an image id); entry shape {fields:{<name>:{value,wording}}, visibleNumbers?:number[], questions?:string[], addressedToAssistant?:boolean, imageText?:string, language?:string}; imageText is only scanned for instructions, never copied into a field. A missing default file test/fixtures/extraction/fake-image-map.json means an empty map (every image is unknown), a malformed file is an error. Providers may implement an optional rephrase({system, content, input, signal}) -> {output:{text}, usage}; the fake does. usage may carry costMicroUsd (integer, preferred by the gate) beside costUsd. User content order in prompt.js is the text block then the image block; the API adapter spec lists image first, so d2 should reorder if the API requires it. ProviderError(code, {usage}) is the only error type the gate and toDegraded understand beyond a generic Error.

The fake parser is a lexicon, not a language model: it handles the documented English and Arabic forms (digits in both scripts, thousands commas, ml/mm, 'by'/'قبل الساعة' with minutes or am/pm, $ / dollars / دولار, pickups / نقطتي) and leaves anything else unknown with a question; a bare hour ('by 11'), Arabic number words other than the dual, and decimals in integer fields are deliberately unknown. EXT-1 corpus texts written in d2 may need lexicon additions in fake.js, which is owned by this task.

The rephrase guard compares against the template sentences, so it cannot catch a reordered comparison or a negation (accepted residual, spec); a capital 'A' or 'I' used as an English article counts as a supplier code and causes a discard (fails safe).

Lesson mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102 (guard root resolution) did not apply: this task builds no hook or guard. The guard itself refused one Bash call (an evidence label containing a greater-than-or-equal sign was read as a redirect to the relative path '='); the label was reworded and the command rerun.
No ECCODE_EVAL line is printed by this task; the fake-mode EXT-1 eval belongs to d2 (test/eval/extraction-fake.test.js).
